  • "One skip warning per conversion." Counting only the table's own plane already counts each lost spectrum once; each plane's warning then names its own.

Known limits.

  • On the separate pass, a repeated position whose second spectrum is empty in the summed table still adds that spectrum's raw points: the pass knows positions, not which spectrum of a position gave the row. The fused route leaves those points out.
  • VAR_BYTES_PER_FEATURE was measured on a grid var. The shared-axis var is built differently and its cost per feature is not measured.
  • A plane the source states but whose every spectrum is empty gets no table and no warning, since the pre-scan never meets it. A spectrum that turns up on such a plane in pass 2 is refused as a disagreement between the passes, as any other is.

docs.title: D59. A FlexImaging run that stopped early is placed by its planned grid
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (2026-10-16), issue #497. Amends D31. D69 extends its overview-photo rule to every optical image with no alignment.

Decision. D31 asks which raster node sits on the .mis reference point: the one that puts every measured spot inside its Area, then the one that leaves the fewest Area nodes unmeasured. Two things change.

  • The search tries every node that keeps each region's spots inside its Area's box. It used to try the 3 nodes either side of a guess made from the spots' centre and the Area's centre.
  • When the source states the grid it planned, that grid chooses among the nodes that keep every spot inside: the node that centres it on the Areas. timsTOF states it as the ImagingArea bounds in GlobalMetadata, rapifleX in the .dat header. A grid is used only when it holds every spot and its size matches the Areas' extent within 1.5 steps. With no usable planned grid, D31's rule chooses. When several nodes still fit equally, the fit keeps the one nearest the old guess and warns that the placement is not determined.

Three related fixes from the same issue:

  • The overview photo. A second optical image is placed by a Scale onto the alignment image only when it is a resampled copy of it: the same ratio on both axes, within the rounding of the copy's sides. Any other image keeps one coordinate system of its own, named after the element, with Identity, and is not in "global", the per-dataset system or "acquisition". A warning says so.
  • The Area's edge tolerance is at least 0.75 photo pixel, besides 0.1 raster step. A .mis stores Area corners in whole pixels, and rounding moves an edge by up to 0.71 pixel. The pixel floor stops at 0.4 step, so on a raster finer than 1.9 pixels per step a whole-step shift still leaves a spot outside.
  • A <ReferencePoint> or Area <Raster> that is not a finite number (inf, nan) is unreadable: the lattice uses the first teaching point, or the Area's own step is dropped.

Why. D31 assumed the spots fill their Area. A run that stops early fills its first rows, and every whole-step shift along the empty part leaves the same nodes unmeasured.

Run Acquired Before After rapiflex_dat_profile_a 6 of 118 planned rows 112 nodes tie; kept one 59 rows low planned grid: one node, its centre 0.4 step from the Area's timsTOF TSF, same slide as timstof_tsf_centroid_a 273 of 2,448 planned spots kept a node 24 rows off the node the complete runs on that slide use timsTOF TSF, same slide 12,867 of 29,939 planned spots kept a node 48 rows off the same node timsTOF, 30 um, one freehand Area 71,249 spots, rows 179-373 of 179-657 the only fitting node lay 14 x 38 nodes from the guess; kept one with 1,550 spots outside that node, every spot inside, found with or without the planned grid

The three timsTOF runs also show what the ImagingArea bounds are: they span every planned row while the frames cover only the first ones, and 51 x 48 nodes is exactly the 2,448 spots FlexImaging planned.

The planned-grid rule assumes that on the right node the grid's centre lies within half a step of the centre of the Areas' box. A whole-step shift then moves it more than half a step away. On rapiflex_dat_profile_a the two centres were 0.4 step apart.

On six complete runs the affine is unchanged to the last digit: tims_msms_pos_brain1 and two runs beside it, timstof_tdf_centroid_a, timstof_tsf_centroid_a and one more complete TSF run. The two public MassIVE runs still land on flexImaging's spot list.

The overview photo of tims_msms_pos_brain1 is the alignment scan turned by about 0.47 degrees. Its two scales were 4.012 and 4.100, and the Scale left it up to 297 photo pixels off at the corners. On rapiflex_dat_profile_a the scales were 2.013 and 2.096, a turn of about 1 degree. The quarter-size _0001 scan is 4.000 on both axes and is still scaled.

On timstof_tsf_centroid_a the old tolerance flagged 28 of 1,599 spots as outside the Area, the furthest 0.38 pixel out. Now none are, and the affine is unchanged. So a complete run that used to warn about spots outside its Area, from corner rounding alone, no longer does.

What changes in a store.

  • A FlexImaging run that did not fill its Area: the TIC image's transform, the pixel polygons, the crop window and raster_to_global_affine. With apply_optical_alignment=False, the photo's place in micrometres.
  • A second optical image that is not a resampled copy of the alignment image, such as the FlexImaging overview photo: its transformations. An mzPeak archive's extra images follow the same rule.
  • A non-finite reference point is no longer copied into the raw .mis metadata.
  • A complete run whose Area holds its spots one way only: nothing.

The objection. Register the overview photo onto the alignment scan from its pixels, so it stays placed. It did not win. It means decoding both photos before the store is declared, against the bounded memory the optical path keeps. A feature fit is random, so two conversions would differ. It would need scikit-image as a declared dependency. And the overview is a coarser copy of the alignment scan, which is placed.

A second objection: with no planned grid, anchor the run at the Area's first node, where FlexImaging starts. It did not win either. On rapiflex_dat_profile_a the first planned column was never acquired, so that anchor is a step off.

Known limits.

  • The planned grid is taken to cover every Area in the .mis; a grid of another size is not used. Every partly acquired run measured had one Area.
  • The size check allows 1.5 steps. A grid planned with a margin column on both sides of the Area fails it, and the fit falls back to D31's rule and its tie warning: safe, but the grid goes unused.
  • Where the Areas' centre sits exactly half a step from both of two nodes, the planned grid ties too, and the fit warns.
  • A square overview photo has the same ratio on both axes at any turn, and is still scaled.
  • The search tries at most 250,000 nodes per pair of axis directions. Past that, or when no node keeps the spots inside the Areas' box, it tries the 3 nodes either side of a seed: the node that centres the planned grid on the Areas when there is one. Without one the seed is the old guess, as before, which on a run that stopped early in a large Area can miss the right node; the fit then warns that spots fall outside, or that the placement is not determined. When no node keeps every spot inside, a first pass over the edge spots may miss the node with the fewest spots outside; the fit warns either way.
  • Below 1.9 photo pixels per step, whole-pixel corners can still trip the warning about spots outside the Area.
  • A planned grid cannot tell a mirrored stage from the usual one. With one, the usual axis directions are preferred before the grid is consulted.

docs.title: D60. A damaged isolation window is left out, and an isomer's label is its rank
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (2026-10-16), issue #498.

Decision. Three rules for the MS/MS schedule.

  • The timsTOF reader screens every isolation window it reads, from PasefFrameMsMsInfo, the DIA tables or FrameMsMsInfo. The target must be a finite m/z above 0; a NULL target (which is also how SQLite stores a NaN) is no target. The width, when the row has one, must be finite and not negative. The collision energy must be finite, of either sign, since the schema sets it no bound and signed energies exist. A PASEF or DIA scan range must ascend from 0. A row that breaks one of these is left out of the schedule, with one warning that counts them. The table the frames use is still the first one with rows (D37): when none of its rows is usable, the schedule records the MS level with no windows, and the next table is not asked. Isomer windows are listed by m/z, then by first scan descending, which is 1/K0 ascending on the TIMS ramp: the order the _msms table ranks them in.
  • A window left out that still occupies a usable scan range stops the precursor split: no _msms table is written, with a warning. Its scans still hold the ions it isolated, and splitting by the windows that are left would put those ions in no precursor. This qualifies D2: the split is lossless only when every window of the schedule is kept, so a schedule the screen has cut is refused like any other that does not qualify. A left-out window with no usable range occupies no known scans, and the split goes ahead.
  • The metadata builder screens each window it is given the same way for the target, the offsets and the energy, and skips a bad one instead of failing the whole msi_metadata block. A bad scan range there drops the range from the window, as it did before, not the window. The Waters reader no longer reports an infinite precursor or energy.
  • In an _msms table, two windows at one m/z (an isomer pair) are told apart by their rank in mobility among the windows of that m/z, over the whole schedule. Every column of the second isomer ends in _1, the third in _2, and so on. The first isomer has no suffix.

Why. The schedule was stored as read. On a damaged analysis.tdf, an infinite target became a precursor_mz that thyra validate refuses, a negative target was stored as a precursor, an infinite energy wrote the token Infinity into the document, which strict JSON parsers reject, and one negative width made the builder raise. The assembler caught that and logged it, and the store had no msi_metadata at all, at exit 0.

The suffix used to come from a collision: only a mass bin that both isomers held gave the second one _1. In a bin only the second isomer held, its column had no suffix and took the first isomer's name. So p500_mz2209 named the isomer at 1/K0 1.092 in one store and the one at 1.821 in another store of the same schedule. A join on the label merged two different isomers, and anndata.concat(join="inner") drops precursor_mobility, so nothing showed it. The docstring already said the suffix followed mobility order; now it does.

What changes in a store.

  • A store whose source has a bad window: the window is gone from ms_analysis.fragmentation.windows, and the msi_metadata block is there where it was missing. Where the window still occupies its scans, the store has no _msms table; where it does not, the table holds the other windows.
  • An _msms table with an isomer pair: the second isomer's columns in bins it alone holds gain _1. Columns in bins both hold, and every column of a schedule without isomers, keep their names. With three or more windows at one m/z, a bin held by the first and third gives the third _2, where it was _1.
  • A schedule with an isomer pair: uns["msms_schedule"] and fragmentation.windows list the pair by 1/K0 ascending (first scan descending), where SQLite's grouping order (width, energy, then first scan ascending) listed them before. Window 0 of the schedule is now the isomer without a suffix.
  • No msi_metadata field changes shape, so the schema version stays.

Alternatives.

  • "Refuse the source." One damaged window out of a schedule is not a reason to lose the conversion, and the warning names the count.
  • "Clamp a negative width to 0." That invents a value the source does not state.
  • "Suffix by the isomer's scan range." A rank needs no other value in the label and is the order the docstring promised.

Known limits.

  • The screen tests the numbers, not whether they make sense together: a window far outside the acquired mass range is kept.
  • A left-out window whose scan range is itself unusable gives no scans to reason about, so the split goes ahead; if it did isolate ions, they are in no precursor column and demultiplexed_current falls below 1 with its usual warning.
  • A value bad in some frames only splits one window into groups, and the schedule then reads as varying, so no _msms table is written.
  • The stem kept six significant digits (p{mz:g}), so any two targets that rounded alike, at any m/z (798.5401 and 798.5404 were both p798.54), shared a stem and were ranked as isomers. Since D67 the stem writes the m/z exactly, and only targets with the same m/z are ranked.
  • Leaving an isomer out (a bad window, or a region= store whose region lacks it, D57) re-ranks the other one.

docs.title: D61. An mzPeak TDF frame sums only measurements into a TOF bin
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (2026-10-16). Amends D33, and applies D55's rule to the mzPeak reader's own grouping.

Decision. When the mzPeak reader puts a TDF archive's raw counts on the .d's scale (D33), it sums the points of one frame that fall on one TOF bin. A point whose m/z is not finite, or whose count is not finite or is negative, now joins no bin. It is passed on by itself, scaled but not rounded, and the converter drops, counts or refuses it as it does any other such point. A NaN m/z was already dropped earlier, as null-pair padding.

Why. The grouping split two sorted points when their step exceeded 1e-12 x m/z. Relative to an infinite m/z no step is large enough, so an inf point joined the largest finite bin. Its count was added there and kept at that finite m/z, with or without an intensity threshold. Two -inf points were summed into one. A NaN count made its whole bin NaN, and the converter then dropped the bin's real signal with it. A negative count shrank the bin it joined. D55 fixed the same split test in summed_peak_mask; this grouping is its own copy of the rule.

Measured on a two-pixel fixture at 100 ms, so counts keep their values. Its first pixel holds 2, 3 and 5 at m/z 100, 101 and 102 and one extra point. Values stored for that pixel, resampled to 99.5-102.5, no threshold. A converter-level test holds each "Now" row, and the warning that says the extra point was dropped:

Extra point Before Now 7 at m/z inf 2, 3, 12 2, 3, 5 NaN on m/z 100 -, 3, 5 2, 3, 5 -4 on m/z 100 (bin of 9) 5 at m/z 100 9 at m/z 100

What changes in a store. Only stores of TDF-sourced mzPeak archives with a non-finite m/z, or a non-finite or negative count, on a frame. Their bins hold the measured counts alone. With --intensity-threshold, the points passed on decide nothing either: the threshold, applied after this step, leaves them out of every sum (D55). Without resampling, a non-finite m/z is refused as before, since it would become var["mz"]. Archives whose m/z and counts are all finite and non-negative give the same stores, value for value. A count between -0.5 and 0 used to round to 0; it is now passed on unrounded and dropped with a warning. Real TDF counts are unsigned, so no real archive holds one. No schema change.

Alternatives.

  • "Drop such points in the reader." Then the converter could not count or refuse them, and a non-resampled conversion would quietly lose a point it refuses on every other route. D55 rejected the same option.
  • "Reuse summed_peak_mask." It returns a keep mask, not the summed bins, so it cannot replace this step. The two share the tolerance (SAME_PEAK_RELATIVE) and now the rule for what counts.

docs.title: D62. A NaN or an infinity from the vendor metadata is left out of the metadata block
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (2026-10-17). Applies D55's rule, that a non-finite value decides nothing, to the msi_metadata block. D60 did the same for isolation windows. No schema version change.

Decision. The block holds finite numbers only. JSON has no NaN or infinity, so the published JSON Schema never allowed them; the models now agree with it.

  • The builder leaves such a value out. The mobility range is kept with both edges finite or not at all; its scan count likewise. A processing parameter that is not finite is left out of its step. An isolation window with one is left out whole, as D60 decided.
  • A pixel size is refused, since the block requires one. convert_msi refuses a detected pitch that is not a finite number above 0, as it refuses a missing one, and asks for --pixel-size. The converter refuses such a pixel_size_um or detected y pitch. A converter built without a pitch keeps its default when the source's is unusable, and says so; the store records the pitch as default. thyra metadata leaves the pitch out, as D23 does for a source with no raster.
  • The Python API refuses a non-finite setting, as the CLI already does. That is intensity_threshold and every number in resampling_config. No summed peak reaches a NaN or +inf threshold, so either one emptied the store while the step recorded the threshold. -inf kept everything.
  • The models refuse NaN and infinity (allow_inf_nan=False on every schema model), and to_uns_dict packs its JSON strings with allow_nan=False.
  • thyra validate reports a stored one as an error, once per value, at its location. The message says that converting the source again leaves the field out. The exit status is 1.

The order is the point. The uns assembler catches the models' error, so refusing at the models alone wrote the store with no msi_metadata block and one warning, while the conversion reported success. A converter test pins that the block is still written.

Why. #494 refused these values where a JSON document is read or written. A conversion still stored them, because the models took them. A gt=0 bound refused NaN but not +inf; an unbounded field took all three. thyra metadata and thyra export-metaspace then refused to write the store's own metadata as JSON.

What changes in a store. Only stores whose vendor metadata or API settings held a NaN or an infinity in one of these fields. The field is now absent instead. A pitch like that now stops the conversion with a message, where it used to reach the store. The problem was found by a stress test; no real dataset is known to hold one. Every other store is unchanged.

Why no schema version change. The published JSON Schema is the same file: pydantic writes nothing for allow_inf_nan, and a JSON document cannot hold NaN anyway. Every JSON document that validated still does. Only a Zarr store, whose attributes can hold a NaN float, could have one.

Why thyra validate errs rather than warns. Such a block does not conform to the schema it names, and a strict JSON reader of it fails. A warning would pass it through a CI gate that exists to catch that. The remedy is the user's own: convert again.

Alternatives.

  • "Refuse the conversion when a vendor value is not finite." One optional field would then block a conversion whose spectra are fine. D60 took the same view for isolation windows. The pitch is the exception, because the block cannot be written without one.
  • "Store null." The block's convention is that a field the source does not report is absent, not null.
  • "Coerce to a finite stand-in, such as 0." That invents a measurement.

docs.title: D63. An imzML states z on every spectrum or on none
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (2026-10-19), issue #521. Amends the imzML half of D30.

Decision. Every spectrum's z is judged the way the parser reads it: a cvParam IMS:1000052 with a value, on the scan itself. A term with no value counts as no z.

  • A file that states z on some spectra and not on others is refused, with the mzPeak route's sentence: "A plane is stated for every spectrum or for none."
  • A file whose scans take z from a parameter group is refused by name. The parser would give those spectra its stand-in 1 and sum the planes.
  • Every spectrum states z: D14 applies as before. None does: D30 applies, and the z offset is 0.

The judgement costs no second pass. A hook on the parser's own pass over the spectra records one byte per spectrum, as the polarity hook of D55 does. D30's sentence about reading the first spectrum again is replaced.

Why. Reading only the first spectrum went wrong four ways, all at exit 0. The recorded offset depended on spectrum order. A term with no value counted as stated. The stand-in 1 formed a plane of its own: 11 rows on one plane, 1 on another. Two planes stated through groups were summed into one table. Meanwhile the archive of the same file was refused, or got another offset.

The same hook names what the parser cannot read. A position held in a parameter group or in a second <scan>, a position that is not a whole number, and an array read through a group the parser did not pick each ended in a raw TypeError, ValueError or AttributeError traceback. Each is now one ConversionRefused naming the spectrum and the cause. A document that is not well-formed XML, or is empty, gets the same, naming the file. The position cases are refused rather than read, as the z case is.

The objection. Convert such files with the unstated spectra on plane 0. It lost: that mixes planes from stated and unstated z, and the two routes would still differ. A refusal costs only hand-made files. Every public example and test fixture states z on all spectra or on none, and none through a group.

What changes in a store. Files that mix stated and unstated z, or hold z in a group, stop converting; no store is written. A file whose z terms all lack a value records z offset 0 instead of 1. Every other store is unchanged.

Known limit. The hook wraps a private pyimzml method, as D55's does. The z tests convert files through it, so a pyimzml release that renames the method fails there.

docs.title: D64. imzML arrays: precision on the first spectrum, byte ranges on every spectrum
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (2026-10-19), issue #521.

Decision. Thyra refuses an imzML whose binary arrays overlap in the .ibd, on any spectrum. Two arrays of the same kind may point at exactly the same bytes, as a continuous file's shared m/z axis does. Thyra also refuses a file whose first spectrum has an array whose own precision term disagrees with its param group, whether or not the array states IMS:1000104. An ion mobility array declared as 16-bit float (MS:1000520) is read as 16-bit; a precision Thyra cannot decode is refused by name.

Why. The parser reads each array at its group's precision and never looks at a term on the array itself. It also reads as many values as a spectrum states, wherever they end. A spectrum that stated four values and stored three read into the next array, and an invented m/z of 134,217,760 joined the mass range at exit 0. A 32-bit array on spectrum 0 was stored as 514 instead of 15. A 16-bit mobility array was read as 64-bit, from the neighbouring bytes.

Cost. The overlap check needs only the offsets and lengths the parser already holds: 0.46 s on a 918,855-spectrum file whose parse takes about 115 s. Checking every array's precision would need a second pass over the document (73.6 s on that file), and a per-array precision conflict has only been made by hand.

What changes in a store. No store of a well-formed file changes. A file whose arrays overlap, or whose first spectrum has an array that contradicts its group, converted with invented or wrong values and is now refused. A 16-bit mobility array now stores its own values.

Known limits. A later array that states its own precision, and a later spectrum that states fewer values than it stores (a gap, not an overlap), still convert wrong at exit 0. A resampled m/z axis whose source range starts at 0, on a logarithmic or inverse law, still ends in a raw error in the axis planner; that belongs to the resampling fix, not this one.

docs.title: D65. The imzML head is trusted only when its declarations fit together
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (2026-10-19), issue #521. Amends D14.

Decision. The preview and the metadata document describe an imzML from its head only when it declares at least one spectrum, both raster sides are at least 1, the count is no larger than the raster, and the first spectrum sits at x >= 1 and y >= 1. Any other file takes the full read, as a conversion does. A count equal to the raster is a full raster and is trusted.

Three smaller reads of the head follow the same rule, that the preview says what a conversion would read:

  • The pixel size is read where its value is. A size stated through a parameter group that the scan settings reference takes its name and unit from that group too. The preview reported such an area, or a nanometre value, as micrometres.
  • The last array ends at its offset plus its count times its width. A wrong encoded length on a complete file made the preview call it truncated, while the conversion read it.
  • The observed m/z terms are matched as XML. Attributes in any order, either quote, space around =, and nothing inside a comment.

A pixel size in a unit Thyra cannot convert is not read: the log names the unit and a conversion asks for --pixel-size, as on the mzPeak route. It used to be refused, so the file could not be converted even with the flag.

Why. pyimzml's writer declares the largest coordinate, not the count, and the head read stops at the first spectrum. So a 0 that first appeared later went unseen: a 4 x 3 file listed from its last pixel previewed as 3 x 2. A count larger than its raster, or a side below 1, describes no acquisition, and checking both costs nothing. Reading every position instead would give up the header-only speed (0.4 ms against 64 s on a 2.0 GiB file).

What changes in a store. None from the head rule: no conversion reads the head. A file with a pixel size in an unknown unit now converts when --pixel-size is given.

D14, amended. D14 says only the mzPeak extractor reads IMS:1000042 / IMS:1000043; the preview reads them too, under this rule. The rebasing line D14 describes is now logged once per file, naming each axis's base.

Known limit. A wrong count that still fits its raster (too low, or a file cut short after the count was written), and a 0-based file whose spectra fit inside the declaration with its first spectrum away from 0, are still described from the head. Both touch only the preview and the metadata document, never a store.

docs.title: D66. A timsTOF store records the calibration Bruker's library applied
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (2026-10-19), issue #518. Qualifies D46 for TDF: the axis values are the first frame's, and a frame with a TIMS calibration of its own is converted with it. No schema version change.

Decision. Five rules, each so that the store says what the library did.

  • Each frame takes its own 1/K0. Bruker's library turns a frame's scan numbers into 1/K0 through the TimsCalibration row it applies to that frame. When the frames take more than one row between them, each frame's points are converted with the library's call for that frame, as its m/z already are. The mobility table, the mass-mobility heatmap and the mobility grid all take these values, and the range they bin over is widened to every frame's own first and last scan. When every frame takes the same row, the axis is used as before. When which rows apply cannot be told (the library applied a state Thyra did not find, or a mapping cannot be read), every frame is converted for itself, which is exact whatever the rows are.
  • The recorded row is the applied one. uns["mobility_axis"]["calibration"] holds the row the library applied to the first frame, the frame the axis values come from: the applied calibration.sqlite state's row, or the analysis database's row for that frame. New keys say which: frame_id, stored_in (calibration.sqlite or analysis.tdf), calibration_state_id when a state applied, and n_frame_calibrations, the number of rows the file's frames use. It used to be the analysis database's first row whatever was applied. When the applied state is unknown, no row is recorded.
  • A state is named as applied only when the library applies it. The library applies the newest state whose FrameMzCalibrationMapping (and, on a TDF, TimsCalibrationMapping) names exactly the acquisition's frames. A newer state that maps one frame too few or too many is skipped and the one before it applied; with none left, the analysis database's calibration is. Thyra now reads the mappings the same way, and checks its answer against the library's has_recalibrated_state once the file is open. When the library applies none, no state is named. When it applies one that Thyra did not find, the m/z calibration step leaves calibration out, as it does for an unreadable file. When a mapping cannot be read, the newest state is taken, as before.
  • A missing CalibrationInfo costs only the software version, and a calibration.sqlite with no state names the analysis database in the m/z calibration step.
  • TSF or TDF is decided in one place, and the metadata takes the reader's answer. analysis.tsf wins when both databases hold data; a 0-byte one gives way to the other.

Why. Measured with the bundled library on copies of synthetic_tims.d. A state mapping one frame too few, or a frame the acquisition lacks, is skipped: the m/z were the state before it, or the analysis database's, while the store named the newest. On tims_msms_pos_brain1 the only state maps the 713 frames to 300 distinct TIMS rows; a frame's 1/K0 sat up to 9e-4 (about three scans) from the first frame's. Every default conversion of a real TDF with a calibration.sqlite therefore binned later frames on the first frame's ramp. With --no-recalibrated every frame took one row, and the two stores still recorded the same coefficients. The pea and Xenium TSF folders hold a 0-byte analysis.tdf, so their stores said bruker_tdf with ion mobility present, while the spectra were read from analysis.tsf.

What changes in a store.

  • A TDF converted with the recalibrated state on, whose state maps frames to more than one TIMS row (every real one checked): the mobility table, the heatmap, the grid and their bin edges move by up to a few scans' width. The summed table does not change.
  • Every TDF: uns["mobility_axis"]["calibration"] gains the four keys, and its coefficients are the applied state's when a state applied.
  • A source whose newest state the library skips: format_specific.calibration and the m/z calibration step name the state applied, or none.
  • A TSF folder with a 0-byte analysis.tdf: format_specific says bruker_tsf, and ion_mobility is {present: false}.

The MS/MS table's precursor_mobility stays the first frame's 1/K0 at the window's middle scan: a window has one value, and the first frame's stands for the others, which differ by at most a few scans' width.

Alternatives.

  • "Convert every frame through its own call, whatever the mappings." Exact, but it costs a call per frame for files whose frames all share one row, and changes nothing there.
  • "Record only the coefficients, and leave the axis as it is." The F36 half alone; the frames' points would still be binned on the wrong ramp.
  • "Name the newest state, and say the library may have skipped it." A store should say what was applied; the library answers it.

docs.title: D67. An MS/MS label carries its precursor m/z exactly
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (2026-10-19), issue #518. Amends D60's known limits. Keeps D60's rank rule for isomers.

Decision. The stem of an MS/MS column label is p followed by the shortest decimal that reads back as exactly the stored precursor m/z (Python's repr, a trailing .0 dropped). The merged-precursor warning spells m/z values the same way. Two precursors with different m/z always get different stems. Only precursors with the same m/z (isomers kept apart by mobility) share one, and they take the _1 suffix in mobility order (D60).

Why. D2 named labels after the m/z so that anndata.concat cannot put two precursors in one column. At six significant digits (p{mz:g}), precursors 1 to 10 ppm apart shared a stem and were ranked as isomers, so one label could name different precursors in two stores: 798.5401 and 798.5404 were both p798.54, and the second took _1 only in a store that also held the first.

What changes in a store. Only labels that were rounded change: p1179.73_mz… becomes p1179.731_mz…. Exact ones such as p936.578 and p500 keep their spelling, and so do all the labels of tims_msms_pos_brain1. Joining an old and a new store of one run on labels drops the changed columns; align on (precursor_mz, precursor_mobility), as the docs already say.

Alternatives.

  • "Keep six digits and document the limit." No store change, but the docs' promise that a label names one precursor stays untrue.
  • "Fixed decimals, for example four." Uniform, but nearly every label changes.

docs.title: D68. A timsTOF source that Bruker's library must write into has to be writable
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (2026-10-19), issue #518. Stored data does not change.

Decision. Before the library opens a .d, Thyra reads the header bytes of each database it will open: the analysis database always, and calibration.sqlite when the recalibrated state is on. If one is in WAL mode and the .d folder cannot be written (tested by creating and removing an empty folder; a warning names it if it cannot be removed), the conversion stops with one line. The line names the database and says to copy the .d somewhere writable, or, for calibration.sqlite alone, to pass --no-recalibrated. The docs say that the library's -shm and -wal files appear in the .d during a run and can be left by a hard stop. thyra metadata opens no library and is not checked.

Why. The library opens a WAL database read-write in place and puts -shm and -wal files beside it while it runs; every real calibration.sqlite checked is in WAL mode, and so is the pea analysis.tsf. In a folder it cannot write, a run ended in a traceback, or exited 0 with the recalibrated state silently not applied while the store named it. Checked on a copy of synthetic_tims.d with a deny-create permission on Windows: refused in one line, exit 1, no output and nothing new in the .d; --no-recalibrated converted.

Alternatives.

  • "Document only." A read-only source would still fail with a traceback, or convert with a state silently not applied.
  • "Open a temporary copy of the sqlite files." The source would stay untouched, but it costs a copy per run, possibly of the multi-GB binary on Windows. It waits until a measurement on a real read-only share shows the refusal is not enough.

docs.title: D69. An optical image is stored as its file shows it, and placed only where the store aligns it
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (2026-10-19), issue #524. Generalises D59's rule for the overview photo, and amends D29, D33 and D48 where they place an unaligned image.

Decision. Four rules for every optical image a conversion stores.

  • Placement. An image is in "global" and the dataset's coordinate system only when the store holds an alignment for it: the image the .mis (or an archive's teach points) names, once the TIC-to-image affine is built, and a resampled copy of it, scaled onto it. Every other image gets one coordinate system named after its element, with Identity and nothing else. That covers a photo beside a .d with no .mis, a .mis image whose alignment failed, every archive image with no teach-points affine, and the copies of an alignment image that could not be aligned. alignment_element still names the image the .mis designates.
  • Orientation. An image whose file carries an orientation tag (EXIF and TIFF tag 274) other than 1 is stored upright: turned, and mirrored where the tag says so. A quarter turn swaps height and width. The alignment image and its resampled copies are the exception: they stay as encoded, and the conversion warns. optical_images.elements.<name>.orientation records tag and applied on each element whose file carries a tag from 2 to 8.
  • Decoding. A file that starts like a TIFF is read by tifffile, whatever its suffix or declared media type. A TIFF's colour model is applied: a palette becomes RGB, inverted grey is turned back, CMYK and uncompressed YCbCr become RGB. A colour model Thyra cannot turn into grey or RGB is skipped with a warning. A TIFF whose channels span several pages (an OME-TIFF) is stored with all of them; a z stack or time series keeps its first plane, with a warning. A PNG with 16 bits a colour sample is decoded at full depth by imagecodecs, with its own channel count.
  • Names. The part of an element name after <dataset_id>_optical_ keeps only lower-case ASCII letters, digits, _ and ., has no dot at either end, and is at most 30 characters. A second file whose name cleans to a taken one gets _1, _2 and so on, inside the 30. A second file with the same stem (one picture saved as .tif and .jpg) still replaces the first, with a warning, unless the first is the alignment image: then it gets a numbered name (D75).

Three related fixes from the same issue. An archive image that cannot be copied out (a damaged member, a name the disk refuses) is skipped with a warning naming the member. A PNG whose header declares more pixel data than its file can hold, or any whole-page decode larger than the free memory, is skipped before the store declares it. Skip warnings name the archive member, not a temporary copy.

Why. Identity to "global" drew an unaligned photo at 1 micrometre per photo pixel over the MSI data: the public desi_colad_centroid archive's 1,920 x 1,200 px photo covered 1.92 x 1.2 mm of a 13.2 x 13.6 mm image. That placement is a guess about the frame, the kind D29 declined for an archive's own affine. The decoder ignored orientation on the TIFF route, and Pillow applied it to a TIFF on some compressions only, so a camera photo was stored sideways and the same bytes gave two stores under two suffixes. Palette TIFFs were stored as indices, 16-bit colour PNGs as their high bytes, and an OME-TIFF as its first channel, all at exit 0. Names could collide (one image replaced another), end in a dot (Windows drops it, so the root attrs named a missing element), or hold a character spatialdata refuses, which failed the whole conversion.

Why the alignment image is not turned. Nobody knows whether a .mis states its teaching points against the encoded or the upright pixels, and no tagged FlexImaging file exists to check. Turning the pixels alone could break the alignment; keeping them as encoded cannot.

What changes in a store. Only stores with optical images. An unaligned image leaves "global", the dataset system and "acquisition"; its pixels do not move. A tagged non-alignment image is stored upright. A palette, inverted-grey, CMYK or YCbCr TIFF, a multi-page OME-TIFF and a 16-bit colour PNG change pixels, dtype or channel count. An element whose name held a character outside the new set, ended in a dot, or clashed with another changes name, in optical_images and reference_element too. Aligned grey and RGB single-page images, the TIC, the pixel polygons and the coordinate_systems attr do not change, and convention_version stays 1. No image in the test data, in tims_msms_pos_brain1 or in the public mzPeak archives carries an orientation tag.

Alternatives.

  • "Keep the Identity to global and document it." No store change, but viewers keep drawing a misplaced overlay.
  • "Stretch an unaligned image over the MSI extent." A rough overlay that looks right, and the frame guess D29 declined.
  • "Turn the alignment image too, and its teaching points with it." Right if the points refer to the encoded pixels, wrong if they already refer to the upright ones.
  • "Store every image as encoded, and warn." Alignment-safe, but sideways photos stay sideways.
  • "Refuse a name clash." One stray file name would block the conversion.

docs.title: D70. An mzPeak archive leaves MSn out per pixel, and no chunk loses a point
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (2026-10-19), issue #522. Amends D28 and D29. Amended by D73: the imzML route applies the same MSn rule, which ends its first known limit.

Decision. Five rules for the mzPeak reader.

  • MSn spectra are left out per pixel. A spectrum of level 2 and up is left out where a spectrum of a lower level sits on the same pixel. Level 0 and a null level count as MS1 there. An MSn spectrum on a pixel of its own is kept. The log counts what was left out and what was kept. D29 decided for the whole archive: one MS1 spectrum anywhere left every MSn spectrum out, and only level 1 counted.
  • A region's frame count may count those MSn spectra. A listed region matches when its frames equal the spectra in its box after MSn is left out, or before.
  • A spectrum that is not converted shapes neither the axis nor the range. The raw axis is built from the spectra kept, always. Before, data rows of a spectrum the metadata does not list reached it. The observed mass range counts a spectrum only when it has points in the member that is read; a count column with no value at all counts every spectrum. A kept spectrum whose lowest or highest m/z is null has it taken from its points.
  • An MS-Numpress chunk's ends are matched within its own scale. An end is replaced by its bound when it lies within one over the chunk's scale, and never less than 1e-5. Other encodings keep 1e-5.
  • Padding is a point with no m/z and no intensity, or a zero one. A NaN m/z beside an intensity is passed on, and the converter drops or refuses it by D55's rule, as for imzML. A null m/z beside an intensity of 0 is still padding: MS-Numpress stores a true m/z of 0.0 as its null.

Three kinds of malformed chunk row are refused by name. While reading: an MS-Numpress row whose buffer holds another number of values than it has intensities, at any count, or ends inside its header; and a delta row whose mz_chunk_start is null where its first m/z belongs. At open: a transform column such as intensity_numpress_slof_bytes that holds a value beside intensity. A plain row's null start is only a first point with no m/z, and is read as any such point is.

Why. The 4.3.3 stress test (#427) found each of these converting to a wrong store at exit 0.

Finding Before After MS1 on 3 pixels, MS2 on 4 others, two regions 3 of 7 spectra, one region 7 spectra, regions 0 and 1 MS1 at level 0 beside MS2 on every pixel MS2 summed in: rows of 1003 rows of 3 chunked MS-Numpress, last m/z 51,234.57 30 of 730 counts per pixel 730, as its point twin data rows for a spectrum not listed empty var columns, --no-resample the kept spectra's m/z only peaks-only spectrum in a profile archive 89,000 bins over 60 to 505 1,000 bins over 500 to 505 null lowest_observed_mz, first m/z 0.0 low peaks dropped by the default axis row sums as the imzML NaN m/z with intensity 50 dropped as padding, at exit 0 refused on --no-resample, as imzML

An MS-Numpress value is stored as the whole number nearest to it times the scale, so it decodes within half of one over the scale. mzpeak-convert picks the scale that fits the chunk's largest m/z into 31 bits. Above m/z 42,950 that half step can pass 1e-5, and the end kept its decoded value. It then fell outside the declared range, and the default axis dropped it.

The per-pixel rule keeps D29's reason: an MS2 spectrum summed into its pixel's MS1 spectrum was never measured. A pixel with only MSn spectra has no MS1 spectrum to spoil. Leaving it out lost the pixel, and then its region's frame count no longer matched.

What changes in a store. Only archives of the shapes in the table. The MSn rule changes nothing for archives with only MS1 spectra, or with MS1 and MSn on every pixel at level 1. Chunked MS-Numpress archives change only where a chunk's last or first m/z decodes more than 1e-5 off, above m/z 42,950 or so. A NaN m/z with an intensity is now refused with --no-resample and dropped with a warning on a resampled axis.

Alternatives.

  • "Keep the archive-wide rule, and count level 0 as MS1." That still drops every MSn-only pixel, which is the defect.
  • "Allow every chunk 1e-4." A bound that far off may not be the value of that point. One step of the chunk's own scale is the error the encoding can make, and no more.
  • "Count only the regions' spectra before the filter." No Bruker archive with MS1 and MSn on one pixel was at hand to say which count mzpeak-convert writes, so either is accepted.

Known limits.

  • The imzML reader reads no MS level yet. An imzML with an MS2 spectrum on an MS1 pixel still sums it in, while its archive leaves it out. Reading MS:1000511 there needs the parser setup and a group-stated level, and is left to its own change.
  • A null observed bound costs one pass over the signal member when the essential metadata is read. Only archives with such a bound pay it.

docs.title: D71. TIC-preserving resampling keeps the current measured inside the window
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (2026-10-19), issue #516. Extends D13 and D22, supersedes the "share is measured by area" clause of D36 and the tied-m/z clause of D50.

Decision. Seven rules, and two messages.

  • A cropped spectrum keeps the sum of its samples inside the range. When the declared range cuts a spectrum, the preserved total is the sum of its samples inside the range, bounds included: the samples nearest_neighbor keeps. The area share is used only when the range holds no sample at all, a window narrower than the spacing of two samples.
  • Samples outside the range are counted and reported once, as D22 says both strategies do. A window that holds no peak is refused as "every peak fell outside the target mass range", not as an all-zero source.
  • Samples at one m/z are added up first, sorted by value so the sum is the same float in any order. This is what nearest_neighbor does, and what a timsTOF .d folder does per TOF index.
  • When interpolation leaves no bin, each sample inside the range goes to its nearest bin, as nearest_neighbor places it. That happens when every sample falls between two axis points, or when the gap tolerance vetoes every bin. When the range holds no sample, nothing is placed.
  • A spectrum whose largest value is above 2^900 is resampled scaled down by a power of two, then scaled back. Every other spectrum is resampled bit for bit as before. Inside a scaled spectrum, a value more than about 2^1020 below its largest loses precision or reads as zero.
  • The table's average_spectrum divides before it sums in a column whose sum overflows. Every other column is summed and then divided, as before.
  • A range starting at or below m/z 0 is refused on a reflector_tof, orbitrap or fticr axis, and on a tof axis whose law has A = 0, in one line that names where the bound came from. Their bin counts divide by the lower end or take its logarithm, and a centroid source with a peak at m/z 0 ended the default conversion in a ZeroDivisionError. linear_tof axes, and a tof law with A > 0, lay a range from 0, and still do; below 0 they take a square root, so a negative lower end is refused there too. A constant axis lays any range.
  • Messages. A store emptied by --intensity-threshold is refused as "every peak was below --intensity-threshold", not "the reader yielded no spectra at all". The "dropping N empty pixel rows" line counts positions the reader gave no spectrum for apart from measured spectra left empty; only the first can lie outside the acquisition polygon.

Why. The area rule bridged gaps left by --intensity-threshold, or by a profile file that stores only its peaks, with straight lines. The stored total then followed the spacing of the samples, not the ions. On public files the in-window current came out 0.26 to 4.9 times what was measured inside the window, and 126 times on a constructed one, at exit 0; --resample-gap-tolerance changed nothing. A sum is in the same unit as the total it is a share of, matches nearest_neighbor and docs/resampling.md, and the fallback keeps the window between two samples the area rule was chosen for.

Tied m/z made a store depend on the order of the points. Interpolation read one of the tied points and rebinning another, so two scan orders of the same points differed in half the bins, by up to 41 over the full range, and a narrow window stored 706.7, 660.1 or 631.9 for one input. A pixel whose samples all fell between two axis points, under a gap tolerance, was dropped and logged as outside the acquisition polygon. Values near the float64 maximum overflowed the rescale and dropped three of four rows, and made the average spectrum infinite on every route although every stored value was finite.

What changes in a store.

  • X, the TIC image and the average spectrum of every tic_preserving store whose spectra reach past the declared range. That includes the default Waters MRT and rapifleX profile routes with a narrowed window. Each pixel now holds the current measured inside the range, the total nearest_neighbor stores.
  • tic_preserving stores of sources that list one m/z more than once, such as an imzML with one point per mobility scan. A spectrum whose only repeat is a tie no longer counts as a bin to rebin (D50).
  • tic_preserving pixels that were dropped because interpolation left nothing now get a row.
  • Stores with values near the float64 maximum keep every row and get a finite average spectrum.
  • A source with a peak at m/z 0 on a reflector_tof, orbitrap or fticr axis, or a tof axis with A = 0, is refused where it crashed.

A tic_preserving store whose spectra lie inside the range and hold no repeated m/z does not move, and neither does any nearest_neighbor or --no-resample store with finite column sums.

Known limits. A window that holds no sample still takes the area share, which bridges a gap unless a gap tolerance is set. The per-region average spectrum is still summed before it is divided, so it can overflow on such values. On the plan route, the refusal of an m/z 0 bound names the --resample-min-mz flags rather than the plan.

Alternatives.

  • "Keep the area rule but stop it bridging gaps", integrating only across spacings within the gap tolerance. The result would depend on a setting users rarely set, and the default Waters route would stay wrong.
  • "Keep the rule and warn when a cropped run meets gapped spectra." No value would change, and stores would stay wrong by up to 126 times at exit 0.
  • "Divide every spectrum by its largest value before summing." That moves the last bits of every tic_preserving store; a power of two moves none.
  • "Start a source-derived axis at the smallest positive m/z." The planner sees only the source's declared range, so this needs every reader to report the smallest positive m/z; the refusal names the way through.

docs.title: D72. A Cyclic IMS run is read on its own drift axis, and a declared full scan is MS1
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (2026-10-19). Amends D7 and D53. The known limit on regions that do not share one lattice is lifted by D83 (2026-10-22).

Decision. Three rules for Waters runs, each read from the run's own side files:

  • Guard. A run whose header says $$ Instrument: Cyclic-IMS and whose _extern.inf names Acquisition Device: WatersADC has its drift bins read, as a run declaring Acquisition Algorithm: ADC Mode does (D53). Both fields are required. A Synapt G2-Si and an MRT also name WatersADC.
  • Drift axis. Where a function's section of _extern.inf declares IMS Cycle Start Delay and Pushes Per IMS Increment, bin i is stored at (delay + i * pushes) * period ms. The period is the step of the library's getMobility axis. Both fields count pusher periods; the delay's "(ms)" label is wrong. Functions with different timings, a timing that is not two whole numbers of pushes (one field alone, a fraction, fewer than one push per bin), or uneven library steps record no mobility, with a warning, rather than an axis nobody measured. A function without either field keeps the library axis.
  • MS level. A function whose section declares MSMSMode as MS or SIM holds no fragment spectra, whatever precursor its scans report. Any other mode, or none, keeps the D7 rule: a reported precursor means MS/MS.

The store also records what the run declares: format_specific. function_settings (msms_mode, a SIM function's sim_set_mass_mz, ccs_calibration), format_specific.cyclic_sequence (sequence name, IMS cycle time, each step's vendor function code, array mode and time, from the method file <run>.xml), start_delay_pushes and pushes_per_bin in format_specific.ion_mobility, and instrument_model "SELECT SERIES Cyclic IMS".

Why the guard. Every Cyclic run lacked Acquisition Algorithm, so all of them were refused. Measured on 25 Cyclic MALDI acquisitions (cell images at 5, 10 and 20 um, lipid standards, two HDSIM runs; every acquisition in the set but MassLynx's own exports and two empty runs), each read in its own process with the guard lifted: on every checked scan (all of them, or 3,000 spread evenly over the larger runs) the raw bins summed to the profile spectrum with the same m/z points and a largest difference of 0.0. Nothing crashed, and no file in the source folders changed. Over the 695 in-house Synapt directories with drift files, the 35 G1 runs carry neither field (their header names only a serial); the 659 G2-Si runs declare ADC Mode and no Cyclic label.

Why the axis. getMobility gives 0 to 13.133 ms in 0.06600 ms steps on every Cyclic run, one push per bin. MassLynx's own drift-time export of the same runs (*_1_dt.raw, one scan per bin, retention time = drift ms) gives 309.002 to 348.403 ms in 0.19799 ms steps. The function declares delay 4682 and 3 pushes per bin, and (4682 + 3 i) * 0.0659979 reproduces the export on all 200 bins to 1.8e-5 ms (float32 precision), on a full-scan and a SIM run. Synapt runs declare neither field in a function section (only ADC Pushes Per IMS Increment 1 under the instrument configuration), so their axis is unchanged.

Why the MS level. Every Cyclic full scan reports precursorMz 500.0, which is Quad.MSFixedMass; the HDSIM runs report 524.4, the quadrupole set mass. Both report MS level 1 and declare MSMSMode MS and SIM. With the guard lifted, D7's rule stored the full scan as MS2, CID, target 500. No Synapt or Xevo _extern.inf among the in-house runs declares MSMSMode at all, so none of their stores changes.

No CCS. Thyra derives CCS from 1/K0 only (ccs_applies refuses drift time). Every Cyclic run declares CCS Calibration: No, recorded as such. After several passes an ion outside the targeted mobility window can lap the ones inside it, so a multipass arrival time is a drift time only within that window.

What changes in a store.

  • Cyclic IMS runs, which were refused, now convert with uns["mobility_axis"] on the declared timing (309.0 to 348.4 ms, bin width 0.198 ms on the runs measured) and uns["mobility_heatmap"]. Under --waters-spectrum profile the heatmap's current_ratio is 1.0000 and the grid marginal 1.0.
  • A Waters function declaring MSMSMode MS or SIM stores ms_analysis.fragmentation at MS level 1 with no window and no dissociation, and no uns["msms_schedule"]. An excluded such function lists no precursor_mz.
  • A run declaring none of these fields stores what it stored before. That is every in-house Synapt and Xevo run read; no MRT run was re-read.

D7 and D53, amended. D7's "precursor_mz is the field to trust" holds where the function declares no MSMSMode. D53's "equal steps from exactly 0 ms" and "no cyclic IMS image was tested" describe Synapt runs only.

Known limits.

  • A multipass separation's pass count is not a field of the method, so it is not recorded; the sequence steps are kept as the vendor numbers them.
  • A Cyclic run split across functions at the file-size cap (D7) has not been seen: the largest run measured keeps a 2.64 GB _func001.dat as one function. On a Synapt the tail of a split raster has a function section of its own, as the public XS image shows. A Cyclic chunk without one would record no mobility, since its timing differs from the first chunk's, and would fall back to D7's precursor rule, so a full scan reporting 500.0 would be stored as MS/MS. Nothing measured has this shape.
  • A Cyclic run whose regions do not share one stage lattice is refused by the raster fit, as any Waters run is. One lipid-standard run with two line scans is.

docs.title: D73. An imzML leaves MSn out per pixel, as an mzPeak archive does
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (2026-10-19), issue #522. Completes D70 for imzML.

Decision. The imzML route reads each spectrum's MS level and applies D70's rule. A spectrum of level 2 and up is left out where a spectrum of level 1, level 0 or no stated level sits on the same pixel. The pixel is the spectrum's x, y and z, so a spectrum on another plane is on another pixel. An MSn spectrum on a pixel of its own is kept. The log counts what was left out and what was kept, as the mzPeak reader's does. Both routes call one function for the rule.

  • The level is read on the spectrum, then in its groups. A spectrum's own MS:1000511 comes first. Otherwise the groups it references are read, the last one listed that states a level, as pyimzml resolves them. A value that is not a whole number, or is below 0, counts as none. A level above 255 is kept as 255, and the log names it so; it is MSn all the same.
  • A spectrum left out is not read. It adds nothing to X, the raw mass axis, the mass range, n_spectra or the peak count. Nor does it add anything to the mobility point clouds or the mobility range, and it is not asked for a mobility array or for one as long as its m/z array. A continuous file takes its shared axis from the first spectrum that is kept.
  • A spectrum keeps its place in the list. obs["acquisition_order"] still counts every <spectrum>, so the spectra after one left out do not move (D26).

Why. The 4.3.3 stress test (#427, F26) converted an imzML with an MS2 spectrum on an MS1 pixel, and its own mzpeak-convert archive.

Input Before After the imzML, level stated on each spectrum TIC 40 and 1280 40 and 80 the imzML, level stated in a group TIC 40 and 1280 40 and 80 its mzPeak archive (D70) TIC 40 and 80 40 and 80

D70 gives the reason for the rule: an MS2 spectrum summed into its pixel's MS1 spectrum was never measured. Reading the level through pyimzml's per-spectrum values does not work. They never follow a group reference, and the pyimzml writer and mzpeak-convert both state the level in a group. The full per-spectrum metadata would follow it, at about 10 GiB on a 918,855-spectrum file. So the level is read in the step that already records each spectrum's z (D63), at one byte per spectrum.

What changes in a store. Only files with an MSn spectrum on a pixel that holds MS1 too. A file with no level, with level 0 or 1 only, or with MSn on pixels of their own converts as before. Before and after were converted from the same tree otherwise: the committed imzML and timsTOF fixtures, two example imzML sets, two profile imzML exports, a 918,855-spectrum imzML and four mzPeak archives. All 17 stores are identical. Reading the levels adds about 3 s to the 46 s parse of the 918,855-spectrum file.

Alternatives.

  • "Refuse an imzML that holds MS1 and MSn on one pixel." Its archive converts, so the two routes would still disagree.
  • "Ask pyimzml for the level with include_spectra_metadata." It misses a level stated in a group, which is where most writers state it.

Known limits.

  • The metadata-only route and a mass axis plan read the imzML header, not the spectra, when the header is enough. Their spectrum count and observed range then still include MSn spectra that a conversion leaves out. A plan's axis can then reach past the converted spectra; no point is lost.
  • format_specific.spectrum_count stays the number of spectra the file holds, as on the metadata-only route.

docs.title: D74. Source keys in uns are stored under path-safe names, and an overflowing grid confirms no pixel size
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (2026-10-20), issue #523. Amends D27.

Decision. Two rules, both about values a source states that Thyra cannot store or test as written.

  • Keys. Every dict key that becomes a node of uns is stored under a name Zarr can hold on every platform. Each /, \, :, *, ?, ", <, >, | or control character, and each dot or space at the end of a key, becomes _. A key that is safe already keeps its name; one that would meet it is given a number, MS_1000529_2. Keys inside a list that is stored as one JSON string are kept as written: any key is legal there. The rule holds for every format, since every reader's metadata reaches uns through one function.
  • Pixel size. A declared pixel count or extent is used to test a lone IMS:1000046 only when it is a finite number above zero, and so is the product of the side and the count. A value that is not a finite number, a whole number too large for a float or a JSON Infinity for one, is ignored with a warning, as a value that is not a number already was.

Why. The 4.3.3 stress test (#427) found both.

Input Before After mzPeak run block with a key MS:1000529, on Windows save fails after the conversion, exit 1, .failed left stored as MS_1000529 index metadata key vendor:note the same vendor_note imaging.notes key a/b save fails: Zarr refuses a / in a key a_b old-name IMS:1000046 10000, count 1e307, extent 1e306 mm 10000 um pixel, logged as confirmed no pixel size: --pixel-size asked for the same, count 1e305, extent 1e307 mm 10000 um pixel no pixel size

A key with a colon is legal on Linux, so the same archive converted there, and its store kept the colon. The extent of 1e306 mm is infinite in micrometres, and isclose(inf, inf) is true whatever the pixel size, so the test confirmed a reading it could not have made.

What changes in a store. Key names, in uns only, for a source whose metadata keys hold one of those characters. The root attributes keep the keys as the source wrote them; there they are JSON keys, legal everywhere. The metadata of 14 local datasets was read and walked as the store writes it: five imzML, four timsTOF (TSF and TDF, one with MS/MS), three Waters (one Cyclic IMS), a PHI ToF-SIMS run and a rapifleX run. No key was renamed. No solariX acquisition or published mzPeak archive was at hand. The pixel size changes only for an mzPeak archive whose declared grid overflows, or that states a pixel size as a JSON Infinity or NaN: such a value was taken as an infinite pixel and is now ignored, so the conversion asks for --pixel-size. No writer is known to produce either.

Alternatives.

  • "Store the free-form blocks as JSON strings, as lists already are." Every block would change its type in every store, to rescue a few keys.
  • "Refuse a source whose keys are not path-safe." The keys are provenance; losing a conversion over one is the wrong trade.
  • "Drop the unsafe characters instead of replacing them." a:b and ab would then meet, and the change would be harder to read back.

Known limits.

  • Two keys that differ only in case are two nodes, which a file system that folds case, as Windows does, puts in one folder. That was so before this rule too. No source with such keys was found.
  • The renamed key is logged at DEBUG only.

docs.title: D75. The photo crop follows the regions converted, and one affine places every region
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (2026-10-20), issue #520. Amends D31 for the fallback without teaching points, and D69's rule for names.

Decision. Six rules for a FlexImaging .mis and the optical alignment it gives.

  • The crop follows the regions converted. Whether the alignment photo is cropped, and where, is decided by the regions the conversion converts, counted from the data or --region, never by how many Areas the .mis maps. One converted region is cropped around its cells as the TIC-to-image affine places them, plus the 10% margin, whether or not it has an Area. Its crop then records region_name null. A run converted whole with several regions keeps the whole photo.
  • A region with no Area is placed, and named. Its pixels, polygons included, are placed by the affine every region shares, and the conversion warns once for each converted region without an Area.
  • One affine, with or without teaching points. Without the D31 lattice, the raster is stretched over the box of the mapped Areas, with TIC cell 0 at the raster's first position. The TIC image, every polygon and the crop all use that one matrix. Before, each region's polygons used its own Area while the TIC used the box, and a lone region ignored where the raster started.
  • An Area that cannot be read keeps its place. It stays in the list with its name and no outline, with a warning, so the Areas after it still pair with their own regions. That covers a point that is not two finite numbers within 1e9, fewer than two points, no width or height, and a polygon whose points lie on one line. A --region name that two Areas share is refused, naming the RegionNumbers that carry it.
  • Teaching points must span the photo. Three points that repeat or lie on one line fix no affine. The lattice is not fitted from them, and msi_metadata.alignment.method is not claimed. A .mis number is read as a finite decimal; a Raster or TeachPoint that is not one is left out with a warning naming it. When the .mis gives no usable Raster, a warning says the pitch is BeamScanSize.
  • The alignment image is the exact file. It is the file the reader resolved from the .mis it adopted, not any file with the same stem. A later file never replaces it: a same-stem file gets a numbered name. When the named file is not there by that exact name, the one image of that name, else of that stem, stands in, as before (scan.tiff for scan.tif); two that match equally are not guessed between. A Rapiflex run reads a .mis only from its own folder, as its reader does.

ImagingArea*IndexPos values are read as exact integers. An empty or NULL value counts as absent, and the frames' own bounds stand in, key by key, in the metadata and in the alignment's first raster position alike. A missing or empty MzAcqRange is a one-line refusal.

Why. The 4.3.3 stress test (#427) found sixteen ways a .mis or its GlobalMetadata reached a store unchecked, all on the synthetic timsTOF and rapifleX fixtures. Among them: one unreadable Area moved every later Area onto the wrong region, so --region gamma converted another region's spectra. With one Area for three regions, the photo was cropped to that one Area, leaving two regions' pixels off the stored photo. Without teaching points, a TIC cell and its polygon sat up to 0.63 steps apart, or three steps when the raster started before its Area. Three diagonal teaching points spread polygons over 1e17 photo pixels. A same-stem .png at twice the size became the alignment image. Bounds above 2^53 grew a 3x2 raster to 5x2.

What changes in a store. Only stores that met one of those cases.

  • A multi-region run converted whole whose .mis maps one Area keeps the whole photo and loses crop. A region picked with --region that has no Area is cropped, with region_name null.
  • Without teaching points: polygons, the TIC transform, raster_to_global_affine and the crop window, for runs with several mapped regions or whose raster starts before its Area. Regions without an Area get polygons.
  • Which spectra --region <name> converts after an unreadable Area. The Area's placeholder, {"name", "unusable"} with no outline, is now in the table's uns["raw_metadata"]["mis_metadata"] (timsTOF) and in a rapifleX store's format_specific_metadata.areas, where the Area was left out before.
  • Which file the alignment element holds, when a same-stem twin or a parent-folder .mis was there.
  • dimensions and coordinate_offsets_px for bounds above 2^53.
  • msi_metadata.alignment.method for teaching points on one line.
  • Stores that were tracebacks before.

A single-region run, a run with teaching points, and a run whose Areas all read do not change, apart from the cases above.

Alternatives.

  • "Crop a whole multi-region run to the box of all its regions." Every multi-region store would change, and only the two cases above needed to.
  • "Keep cropping to the mapped Areas, and warn." The regions without an Area would still have no photo under their pixels.
  • "Refuse a .mis with an unreadable Area." The other Areas still place their regions, and a placeholder keeps the pairing right.

Known limits.

  • The solariX reader looks for its .mis beside the .d only, while optical discovery also looks inside it.

docs.title: D76. convert_msi refuses every keyword it does not use, and checks its values as the CLI does
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (2026-10-20), issue #519. Extends D10, which answered only sparse_format. Leaves D44's refusal of region as it is.

Decision. convert_msi takes three kinds of argument: its named arguments; the converter keywords its docstring lists (write_mobility_table, mobility_heatmap, mobility_grid, mobility_bins, mobility_min, mobility_max, msms_table, and use_csc for older callers); and, in reader_options, only the documented reader keys (intensity_threshold, use_recalibrated_state, tdf_spectrum, region, use_centroid, spectrum_type, max_mass_axis_length, use_appended_calibration). Anything else is refused before the source is opened, in one ERROR line naming each keyword. A reader key given as a plain keyword is pointed to reader_options.

  • A reader key the format does not use is named, then left out. One WARNING per key, worded as the CLI words its flags (#260). Both routes read one table, READER_OPTION_FORMATS in thyra/reader_options.py. The CLI now hands convert_msi only the options that reach the detected format, so a plain imzML run logs no "is ignored" line although the CLI always sets use_recalibrated_state. region stays refused by a reader that cannot select one (D44): dropping it would convert every region.
  • conversion_options holds only values Thyra computed. A caller's leftover keyword used to be merged in after them, so it could overwrite one, record an option nothing applied, or fail the save after both passes when JSON could not hold it. handle_3d is stored as a plain boolean.
  • The CLI's value checks reach the API. normalize_resampling_config refuses, for a dict and a ResamplingConfig alike: a width, reference m/z, m/z bound, gap tolerance or bins_per_fwhm that is not a positive number; min_mz not below max_mz; a negative TOF law term or a law of two zeros; a bin count that is not a whole number of at least 2. A dataclass with a string method or axis type is read as a dict's is. convert_msi checks the config before it opens the source.
  • Numbers and flags. A pixel size or z spacing is any finite positive real number, numpy scalars included; a bool is refused. handle_3d is a bool, numpy's included. The pixel size is a float from the start, so obs["spatial_x"] is float64 for pixel_size_um=20.
  • Paths and ids. convert_msi refuses an output path under a regular file, or under a folder it cannot write, before it opens the source, with the CLI's message: the check is one function both call. A dataset id may not start with a dot, may not be a Windows device name (nul, con.2), and may hold at most 216 bytes in UTF-8 (216 plain ASCII characters), so its longest element name (an optical image, 39 more) fits the 255 bytes a folder name holds.
  • Dead resampling options are named. Each resampling flag given beside --no-resample gets one WARNING. A gap tolerance under nearest_neighbor is named as ignored instead of logged as zeroing bins.

Why. The 4.3.3 stress test (#427) found ten ways the API and the CLI disagreed (F38, F58, F60, F119, F130, F139, F150, F151, F152, F161). A caller following the rendered API reference passed spectrum_type as a keyword: the option did nothing, and the store recorded it as applied. A negative width gave a 100-bin axis; a gap tolerance of 0 switched the check off while the log said it was in force. An id starting with a dot wrote a store SpatialData's reader opens as empty, since it skips names starting with a dot. Q6 of the stress report weighed refusing, warning, or only dropping the record; refusing was chosen because a misspelt option then cannot give a store the caller did not ask for.

What changes in a store. A call that passes only documented arguments writes the same store, with one exception: the "mass axis resampling" step no longer records a gap tolerance when the method is nearest_neighbor, where it acted on nothing. Ousia's wizard always sends a tolerance, so its nearest-neighbour stores lose that key and its log gains the warning. A call that passed an unknown keyword or reader key, or a value the CLI refuses, now returns False and writes nothing. obs["spatial_x"] is float64 where an int pixel size made it an integer column. conversion_options no longer carries a caller's leftover keywords.

Alternatives.

  • "Warn once per unused keyword and keep it out of conversion_options." Breaks nobody, but a misspelt option still gives a store the caller did not ask for.
  • "Accept in silence and stop recording unused keywords." The store stops contradicting itself, but an option that does nothing passes without a word.

Known limits.

  • A converter class built directly still takes leftover keywords in options; they are no longer written to the store.
  • A Windows device name is refused on every platform, so a store written anywhere can be copied to Windows. An id ending in a dot is not refused; Windows drops the dot from a folder name.

docs.title: D77. A conversion that will not fit is refused before it allocates, on memory and on disk
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (2026-10-20), issue #528. Extends the mass-axis guard (#251) and D4's reading of free memory; amends D2.

Decision. Five changes, each one line in the log where a traceback used to be.

  • The count ceiling is part of the axis guard. One table counts at most 268,435,456 keys (a 1 GiB uint32 count array). The mass-axis guard now checks that first, so an axis of more bins is refused before it is built, however much memory is free. The count array still raises past the ceiling as a backstop, now as a refusal that is also a MemoryError, so the callers that leave a sibling table out still catch it.
  • The MS/MS table is left out past the ceiling. Precursors x mass bins past 268,435,456 keys is asked when the table is planned. The table is left out with a WARNING naming --resample-bins and --no-msms-table, and the summed table is written, as for the mobility grid. D2 said the default never breaks a conversion; this was the case where it did.
  • Tables and regions count. The projection is bins x (200 + 36 per table past the first + 20 per region when there are two or more) bytes. The regions are known before their arrays are made, and are checked then. The 2D route's tables are known only after the pre-scan, which finds the planes, and are checked then, before the matrix is allocated. Every check compares with the free memory read the first time: before a resampled axis is built, or once a raw axis is handed over. By the later checks the conversion holds part of what the projection counts.
  • Free memory is what this process can take. The smaller of the machine's free memory and a limit on the process: a Windows job object (per process or per job), a Linux cgroup (v1 or v2, every level up to the root) or RLIMIT_AS. A cgroup's reclaimable page cache (inactive_file) is not counted as used. The mobility tables' guards (D4) read the same function.
  • Free disk is checked after the pre-scan. The counted bytes of every matrix about to be allocated (12 bytes per entry, 16 past 2^31 entries), summed tables and the siblings fed from the same passes, are compared with the free space of the output's drive, where the scratch folders go. More than the free space is refused, naming both sizes. More than half of it warns, because the store is written to the same drive while the files exist. A sibling table counted on its own pass meets the refusal when it allocates.

Why. The 4.3.3 stress test (#427) found each case ending in a traceback.

Finding Before After F59: 270M bins, 150 GB free the axis built, then MemoryError refused before the axis F154: 240 precursors x 1.2M bins conversion stopped, no store MS/MS table left out, store written F148: six regions at 5M bins 19.5 B/bin per region not counted counted at 20 F116: ten planes, 2D route 511 B/bin against 200 counted at 200 + 36 x 9 F194: 2 GB job limit, 18M bins admitted, then MemoryError refused, 2.0 GB free F149: matrix twice the drive [Errno 28] after the pre-scan refused after the pre-scan

The per-table figure is the slope of the stress test's measurements: one plane 200 B/bin, ten planes 511. The per-region figure is two float64 arrays per region (the total and the mean, 16 B/bin) plus what building them costs, measured at 19.5. The thresholds for disk follow the memory guard's shape: the matrix files are an exact count, not a projection, so the refusal is at all of the free space; the store is compressed, often to a fraction of the matrix, so its share is a warning.

What changes in a store. Nothing. A conversion that fitted before converts the same way. A conversion that crashed now ends in a refusal or, for the MS/MS table, in a store without that table. A source with many regions or many planes, near the memory limit, may now be refused where it used to be attempted.

Alternatives.

  • "Say in the docs that 200 bytes per bin is per table." It leaves the guard admitting what it knows will not fit.
  • "Refuse the conversion when the MS/MS table is too wide." The grid in the same case is left out, and the summed table is the store's main content.
  • "Read the cgroup's memory.current as used." A source read once fills the page cache, and the guard would refuse a conversion that fits.

Known limits.

  • On Linux the matrix files are sparse, so free space falls only as they are written. The check after the pre-scan counts every file the passes allocate; a sibling table counted later is compared with what is left then, which does not subtract files allocated but not yet written.
  • The fused passes' count arrays for the grid and the MS/MS table (each up to 1 GiB) are allocated before the passes and are not in the projection.
  • The 2D route's plane tables each hold a count array during the pre-scan, 4 bytes per bin, before the table count is known.

docs.title: D78. A folder that holds several runs is refused, not picked
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (2026-10-22), issue #525.

Decision. A run is a .d folder Thyra reads, timsTOF or solariX; other .d folders beside it do not count. A folder that holds one run is read as that run by every entry point: convert_msi, preview_msi, thyra metadata and the CLI, whose --interactive-calibration display now shows for it. A folder that holds several runs is refused by convert_msi, preview_msi, thyra metadata and the timsTOF reader with one line that names every run and asks for one run's path. The CLI still asks which run to convert, and ends with the same line and exit 1 when it can read no answer, where click printed a bare Aborted!. Format detection is unchanged: it still names the first run's format, and only the entry points refuse.

Why. The library converted the first run in name order with one INFO line, so a real folder of three runs gave a store of a run nobody chose, at exit 0. A library cannot ask, and the .mis pick already refuses to guess (#303).

What changes in a store. Nothing. A call on a folder of several runs now writes nothing.
